chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The woman who does not become permissible to her husband until she marries another man?' He said: 'She is the one who is divorced, then reconciled, then divorced, then reconciled, then divorced for the third time; so she is the one who does not become permissible to her husband until she marries another man who tastes her sweetness.'

key_terms.تُرَاجَعُ: She is reconciled/revoked (during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific condition for a woman with three divorces to remarry her first husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the distinction between Talaq al-Munfasikh (irrevocable divorce) and Talaq al-Mujarrada, specifying that a woman divorced three times by the same husband becomes permanently barred to him until she marries another man and consummates the union. The phrase 'tastes her sweetness' (tadhawqu 'usaylataha) is interpreted by Shia scholars as requiring actual sexual intercourse, thereby distinguishing it from a mere nominal marriage (Zawaj al-Tahil) which might not involve consummation. This ensures the second marriage is genuine and not merely a legal formality to permit return.
